The Subtle Art of Slowing Down.

Visual essay · 2025

A personal film about creativity, burnout and the cost of never stopping.

Open on YouTube ↗

I made this six-minute film in August 2025, after a year spent rushing through almost everything.

Deadlines, meals, even the things I was supposed to enjoy. A question from my therapist stayed with me: “You eat fast, don't you, Mattia?”

I recognised the same hurry in the rest of my life. There was little room to notice what I was doing.

I uploaded my first YouTube video at ten. Photoshop, photography, websites, motion design and drawing on Procreate followed. By eighteen, I was working as a freelance filmmaker, photographer and designer in Italy. The things I used to do for fun had become my job. Every finished project led straight to the next one.

I built the mood board from things I’d been saving on mymind for months: colour palettes, images, quotes and references. Fragments collected before I knew what I would use them for.

Writing one page a day, by hand, in Field Notes notebooks also fed into the film.

It remains my most personal project, and the one that connected most with my audience. A film about giving myself permission to pause.
